hook.h2: He told a young king to ask for anything
hook.text: At Gibeon our Father appeared to Solomon in a dream at night, saying, "Ask what I should give you."
hook.note: A new king, an open offer, and no conditions on it. Solomon did not ask for wealth, long life, or the defeat of his enemies — he asked for a listening heart, because he knew the weight of the people he had been given. The verse is worth seeing in His color for one reason: the offer came from our Father first. Leaders who ask are answered.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking. Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

At Gibeon our Father told a young king to ask for anything. Solomon asked for a listening heart to govern the people he had been given, and our Father answered him out loud. Leaders who ask are answered.
That is what this Bible was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has.

Leadership is a job of inputs. Everyone who reaches you wants something, and most of what reaches you has been shaped before it arrives. The one voice that has no agenda toward you is the hardest to pick out, because in every other Bible it is printed in the same ink as the genealogies. Here it is marked, on every page, so the first voice of the day can be His.

It was made for the person who signs the thing — presidents, CEOs, executives, public servants, officers, board chairs, founders, pastors of large staffs — and for the ordinary weight none of them talk about much: the decision that only comes to you, and the people who go home to families that depend on it.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved child. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

An introduction opens each book, a Father's note closes each with a short prayer, and 1,354 notes serve the reader, not the scholar. A presentation page carries their name. Six by nine, hardcover, full color throughout.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

long.h: Decisions come to you that come to no one else. Your Father wants to be the first voice you hear.
body: At Gibeon, a young king was told he could ask for anything. Solomon did not ask for wealth, or long life, or the defeat of his enemies. He asked for a listening heart, because he knew the weight of the people he had been given. “Ask what I should give you.” — 1 Kings 3:5. “Give your servant a discerning heart to govern your people.” — 1 Kings 3:9.
Your Father answers leaders who ask. He gave Solomon what he asked for, and more besides. It is a devotional Bible for daily Bible reading and intimacy with God, so you hear Him for yourself.

Note what Solomon asked for: not an outcome, but the capacity to hear. That is the request this edition was named around, and it is the one request in the story our Father granted without being asked twice.

long.h: A leader reads it as a son, not as a case study
body: Scripture is full of people in authority, and it is honest about all of them. Saul, David, Solomon, Hezekiah, Nebuchadnezzar, Pilate — the record keeps the failures in. There is no leadership program in this Bible, no principles extracted, no chapter of takeaways at the back; it is the whole text in its own order, and it lets the accounts stand as they are.

What it adds is the one thing no other edition shows: where our Father Himself is speaking into those rooms, in the first person, in His own color. Across 5,623 verses. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking.

It is also built to be handed on. Hardcover with a dust jacket, full color throughout, and a presentation page for a name and a date — the kind of book that ends up on a successor's desk rather than in a box.

long.h: A three color Bible: red letter, blue letter, purple letter
body: For a hundred and twenty-five years, the red letter Bible has shown you the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. He has been speaking the whole time. No Bible has ever shown you where.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE. More than one word in four of this Bible is a divine person speaking.

The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation. His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored. Narration stays black. You can see it for yourself before you buy anything: every word is free to read at fathersheartbible.com/read.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: “I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world” (John 17:6). This translation lets the Hebrew and Greek speak the distinction they always made: God as Father, Abba Father, your Heavenly Father — and you, His beloved child.

Notice who, in Scripture, speaks of Him only as a distant deity and never as Father: the serpent in Eden, Pharaoh, the accusers in Job, the tempter in the wilderness. The enemy's strategy has not changed since the garden — to make the Father seem distant, demanding, and disappointed.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

faq.q: What makes the President's Bible different from the other editions?
faq.a: It is the complete Father's Heart Bible™ in Divine Voice Color — the same translation, the same 876 pages, the same 1,354 study notes as every other edition. What is made for a leader is the cover and the pages that open the book: a word written for this reader, and passages on intimacy, identity, and inheritance chosen for where they are. We would rather tell you that plainly than claim notes or prayers that are not in it.

faq.q: Is this the whole Bible, or a selection?
faq.a: The whole Bible. 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses, Genesis to Revelation, nothing abridged — 876 pages of it, in full color throughout.

For a hundred and twenty-five years red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and until now those words were printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. In Divine Voice Color you see who is speaking: our Father's words in BLUE, the Son's in RED, the Spirit's in PURPLE. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation — His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored.

faq.q: Can I read it before I buy a copy?
faq.a: Yes, all of it. Every word of the Father's Heart Bible™ is free to read at fathersheartbible.com/read, in twenty-five languages, with the color on the page exactly as it is in print. English and Telugu can also be listened to. Nobody has to buy anything to receive our Father's voice.

No. It is for whoever carries the decision — CEOs, executives, public servants, military and police officers, founders, board chairs, school principals, anyone whose call affects people who never get a vote on it. The name is the shape of the weight, not a job title.

faq.q: Does it contain leadership lessons or principles?
faq.a: No, and that is deliberate. There is no leadership curriculum, no extracted principles, no takeaways at the back. It is the complete Bible in its own order, with our Father's words marked on every page. The opening pages speak to a leader; everything after Genesis 1:1 is identical to every other edition.

faq.a: It is made for that. Hardcover with a dust jacket, full color throughout, and a presentation page carrying the recipient's name and a date. Order direct and the volume discount runs from 10% at ten copies to 30% at 250, mixing editions freely; shipping is free at any quantity, and for 500 or more you can contact us directly.
